sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Enschede, in Twente, has a policy of pushing parking off the street and into garages. The council adopted the parking tax ordinance for 2026 on 27 October 2025: street parking costs 3.85 euros an hour in area A and 3.45 euros in area B, charged from 09:00 to 19:00, and area A also charges 3.85 euros from 19:00 to 23:00 [0]. A resident permit for one zone costs 268 euros a year in area A and 84 euros in area B, a business permit 745 euros in A and 185 in B, and a passe-partout permit 1,107 euros a year in A [1]. The direction comes from a parking vision proposed by the college in September 2023, building on the 2012 vision and the 2020 mobility vision. It provides for a 1 euro evening tariff in the garages, paid street parking to 23:00, a street tariff 50 cents above the garage tariff, no new street permits in the inner city, blue zones turned into green zones and scan-car enforcement from 2026 [2][3][4]. These were proposals in 2023, and we saw no vote; the 23:00 hours appear in the 2026 ordinance only for area A, and whether the evening garage tariff applies is not confirmed [13]. A proposal for 2025 tariffs of 3.80 euros in zone 1 and 3.40 in the other zones with a garage tariff of 3.30 euros is also a proposal [11].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The big question is a new garage near the station. A proposal of May 2024 asked the council for a credit of 1,116,000 euros, 366,000 euros to study an underground car park at the bus station and 750,000 euros for a station bicycle store, and says a national housing grant leaves 14.8 million euros for the garage and bus station, to be spent by 2035 [7]. About 800 homes were built in Centrumkwadraat in ten years and 1,750 more are planned, and a parking balance of April 2022 found that a new garage becomes necessary between 2025 and 2030 as street spaces are removed [8]. The budget for 2025 to 2028 lists the study as an investment, and a car park building at the Kennispark as delayed pending the Next Twente development [16]. The 2023 vision also proposed to study park-and-ride at Oldenzaalsestraat and Westerval [6]. For the Kennispark, a proposal of July 2023 would let firms meet extra parking demand at the roughly 900 free car parks around the Grolsch Veste, with monitoring by the city and the business association; the decision line in the copy we read was blank [9]. The charging vision for 2022 to 2035 counted about 300 public charge points and estimated about 1,000 needed in 2025 and 3,100 in 2035 [15].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The municipal Parkeerbedrijf runs paid parking on the street and in garages, with garage and park-and-ride tariffs set by the college because of their private-law character and street tariffs by the council [12]. Its operating calculation includes the H.J. van Heek garage, which the municipality adapted for the MST hospital with an investment of over 20 million euros since 2016 [12]. The general garage conditions published on 26 June 2026 name the municipality as operator and admit vehicles up to 5.00 m long, 2.20 m wide and 2,800 kg [14]. Q-Park lists the Q-Park Enschede garage at Zuidmolenstraat with 466 spaces and the P+R Parkweg with 156 spaces, both open round the clock, with a discount for rail travellers; its tariffs did not load [10]. The university campus offers free parking in about 2,551 spaces, according to its mobility plan of 2021 [17].

Our data cover the P+R Parkweg, whose feed gives 145 spaces against Q-Park's 156, for about 60 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 14% on weekdays and 2% at weekends, and it reached full in a single reading on a Monday afternoon. The garages in the centre are not in our data.
